title: RAGFlow agent pipeline -- T1059.007 unsanitized DSL node name stored XSS via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-58579 (CVSS 5.1 MEDIUM),
affecting RAGFlow before 0.26.3.

The agent-update endpoint normalizes a submitted agent pipeline (DSL)
via `normalize_dsl`, which performs only JSON serialization validation
and preserves the submitted NODE NAME verbatim -- no HTML
encoding/escaping. The `dataflow-result` web UI later renders that node
name into its "Rerun from current step" confirmation modal via
`dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, and the frontend's i18next configuration sets
`escapeValue: false`, so the unsanitized value is inserted straight
into the DOM. An authenticated workspace user who can create or edit an
agent can therefore store arbitrary JavaScript in a node name; it
executes in the session of ANY OTHER workspace member who opens that
dataflow result and clicks rerun -- a stored cross-user-trust-boundary
XSS enabling session/token theft and account takeover, not merely a
self-XSS. The advisory does not quote a specific payload string; the
vulnerable mechanism (unsanitized field -> `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` ->
`escapeValue: false`) is what this rule keys on, not a literal example.

Detection logic flags an agent-DSL update whose node-name field
contains HTML/JS-injection markup (an opening tag with an event-handler
attribute, or a `<script>` tag) -- ordinary node names are short,
human-chosen labels with no legitimate reason to contain markup.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor fix (infiniflow/ragflow, via the
merged fix commit and VulnCheck's corroborating write-up), fixed in
0.26.3.
